# Citation

Dinanty, F., and Rachman, F. (2026). QTL Analysis in Sorghum (*Sorghum bicolor* L. Moench): A Review. *Biota: Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu-Ilmu Hayati* 11(1), 27–38. https://doi.org/10.24002/biota.v11i1.10928 (PDF pp. 1–2).

# One-Sentence Summary

This review summarizes sorghum QTL analyses for agronomic, grain-quality and disease-resistance traits and highlights co-localized and stable loci relevant to breeding (PDF pp. 1–12).

# Research Question

Which sorghum traits have been analyzed by QTL methods, what populations and markers were used, and which loci or genomic regions show major, stable or co-localized effects? This paraphrases the review aim (PDF pp. 1–2, 9–10).

# Biological System

The biological system is sorghum (*Sorghum bicolor* L. Moench), described as having 2n = 2x = 20 chromosomes and approximately 252 Mbp euchromatin and 460 Mbp heterochromatin (PDF p. 1).

# Study Design

Narrative review of published sorghum QTL studies for plant height, flowering time, 1000-grain weight, seed length, grain composition and disease resistance (PDF pp. 1–12). A new meta-analysis by the review authors: Not reported, although the introduction describes a goal of synthesizing and meta-analyzing identified QTLs (PDF p. 1).

# Data

The review extracts study-level populations, markers, mapping methods, QTL positions and phenotypic variance explained from prior reports. Examples include F6:8, F3:5, F12 and F7 RIL populations and SSR, INDEL and SNP markers (PDF pp. 2–6).

# Methods

- Describe single-marker analysis (SMA), simple interval mapping (SIM), composite interval mapping (CIM) and multiple QTL mapping (MQM) (PDF p. 1).
- Summarize QTL studies for plant height, flowering time, 1000-grain weight and seed length (PDF pp. 2–6).
- Review grain-quality traits including Fe, Zn, starch, fat, fibre, protein and carotenoid content (PDF pp. 6–9).
- Discuss co-localization, pleiotropic effects and major or stable loci (PDF pp. 9–10, Figure 1, Tables 1–2).

# Software and Versions

The review names mapping methods but does not report a common software package, version or analysis environment across the cited studies. Exact software versions: Not reported (PDF pp. 1–6).

# Important Parameters

Reported parameters include chromosome and map positions, marker types, mapping population, phenotypic variance explained (PVE), LOD or effect measures and environmental replication (PDF pp. 2–10, Tables 1–2). A universal significance threshold: Not reported.

# Inputs and Outputs

Inputs are genotypes from mapped sorghum populations and phenotypes measured for agronomic, quality or resistance traits. Outputs are QTL positions, effects, PVE estimates, candidate or co-localized genes and stable loci across environments or years (PDF pp. 2–10).

# Main Results

The review reports QTLs across multiple sorghum traits and identifies recurring or high-impact regions on chromosomes 6, 7 and 9 in its framing of agronomic hotspots (PDF p. 1). Table 1 summarizes major loci with PVE values of 40.43% for plant height, 42.47% for flowering time and 17.00% for seed length (PDF p. 9, Table 1). The authors interpret co-localization with *Dw3*, *Dw1* and *Dw2* as evidence relevant to trait control, while causal conclusions remain dependent on the underlying cited studies (PDF pp. 2–5, 9–10).

# Assumptions

QTL interpretation assumes that marker–trait associations reflect genomic regions influencing the phenotype and that repeated or co-localized loci may be useful for breeding. Environmental stability must be assessed across locations and years (PDF pp. 2–5, 9–10).

# Limitations

The review combines heterogeneous studies with different populations, marker systems, environments and mapping procedures. The reported QTLs therefore are not directly comparable in all cases, and co-localization does not by itself establish pleiotropy or causality (PDF pp. 2–10).

# Reproducible Implementation Details

No unified genotype matrix, phenotype file, marker-filtering rule, software version, map-construction workflow or meta-analysis script is supplied. Exact implementation details: Not reported (PDF pp. 1–10).

# Relevance to simitall

**Inference, not an author recommendation:** The reported QTL, PVE, marker and population fields could inform simitall schemas for trait-by-locus evidence and cross-study comparison. The paper does not mention or evaluate simitall (PDF pp. 1–12).

# Terminology

- **QTL:** Genomic region associated with a quantitative phenotype (PDF p. 1).
- **RIL:** Recombinant inbred line population used for genetic mapping (PDF pp. 1–3).
- **PVE:** Phenotypic variance explained by a QTL (PDF pp. 2–6, Table 1).
- **Co-localization:** Occurrence of QTLs or genes for different traits in overlapping genomic regions (PDF pp. 9–10).

Primary source: Dinanty and Rachman (2026), cited above. The review’s cited studies are listed in its References section beginning on PDF p. 11. No outside sources were used.
